sections.title: Spin and parity
sections.extract: Spin and parity Spin and parity values are presented with or without parentheses, based on “weak” or “strong” arguments, respec- tively, as adopted in ENSDF [12], but with one important exception. Since, it is a policy of NUBASE2020 to make a clear distinction between experimental and non-experimental information, parentheses are used only when the so-called “weak” arguments are based on experimental observations.

sections.title: Isotopic abundances
sections.extract: Isotopic abundances Isotopic abundances are given in the decay ﬁeld of Table I with the symbol IS and the values were taken from the most- recent publication of Meija et al. [20]. In several cases the IS values are listed in Ref. [20] as an interval [a,b], but in Table I they are given as IS = (a + b)/2 with a variance σ2= (b−a)2/12 (see section 3.2).

sections.title: Year of discovery
sections.extract: Year of discovery Similarly to the previous version of NUBASE [3, 4], Ta- ble I includes information about the year of discovery for each nuclide in its ground or isomeric state. For the former, rec- ommendations by Thoennessen [21] were adopted. Similar criteria were used when assigning the year of discovery for isomeric states.

sections.extract: Averaging procedure and uncertainties It is a policy of NUBASE2020 to use one standard devi- ation as a representation of uncertainties associated with the recommended values. sections.extract: Symmetrization of asymmetric uncertainties Experimental results are sometimes reported in the litera- ture with asymmetric uncertainties, e.g. X+a −b , and it is a policy of NUBASE to symmetrize these uncertainties. sections.title: Rounding policy
sections.extract: Rounding policy In general, values for properties presented in NUBASE2020 and their uncertainties are rounded off, even if unrounded ones were given in the literature or in ENSDF.
